integrity: For zero vertices the half-graph condition is exactly a suffix equation on the B labels or a prefix equation on the A labels. Zeros on both sides force side weights at least two, giving the lower bound four. At equality both side weights are exactly two. If the A support reached any index at least two, b_1 would be positive and then every a_i with i at least two would be forced positive, contradicting side weight two. Thus only a_1 carries A-weight, and the equation at a_n forces b_n to carry all B-weight.
scientific_limitations: The theorem treats canonical half graphs rather than arbitrary chain graphs with repeated neighborhood classes.
The uniqueness statement begins at n=4; H_3 has a second minimum function.
Finite exhaustive verification covers n from two through fourteen only and is corroborative.
A differently phrased or non-indexed half-graph treatment may exist.
title: Perfect Italian domination of half graphs
